title: The flat at a point functor is unchanged by a finite local extension carrying an isomorphic module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the functor of points where a module is flat at a point is unchanged when the local algebra is replaced by a finite local extension carrying an isomorphic module (statement lines 6067-6074, tag 05P4). The proof works after an arbitrary base change: it records that finiteness survives the base change and that the maximal ideal upstairs is the radical of the extended one, uses the latter to identify the closed set of relevant primes upstairs with the preimage of the one downstairs, and then reduces flatness of the localised module to flatness at the maximal ideals of the localisation, which finiteness matches with the primes over the original prime. The comparison of the two vanishing loci is the substance, so the claim is H2.
